analyst_view.overall: Kairat (27th of 36, two points) host Mjällby (9th, seven points) in Almaty and need a win to climb out of the elimination places, under interim coach Zhora Harutyunyan after Rafael Urazbakhtin left in late October. Kairat's domestic season is over, so they come in with about three weeks without a competitive game; their weak recent shooting and leaky defence (14 conceded in six, including 1-5 at home to Panathinaikos) are already in the numbers, and only Jorginho is out. Mjällby are unbeaten in five, flew out on Monday via Istanbul for a week-long trip and still have an Allsvenskan finale at Halmstad on Sunday, so some rotation is possible. Forward Jacob Bergström, one of their two top scorers, went off against Malmö with a thigh problem and FotMob still lists him as doubtful, while Dalsgaard and Stavitski (in the numbers) stay out. Polish referee Paweł Raczkowski's low card record (3.8 a game) is already counted, so the view only trims the shooting a little.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already trim Kairat for scoring only 3 in their last six. Kairat's three-week break could blunt their attack but also loosen a defence that let in five at home to Panathinaikos, while a missing Bergström or a rotated Mjällby side points slightly down, so with these pulling both ways I stay at 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, already cutting Kairat for winning only 12 in their last six and lifting Mjällby a little for 17 in their last three. Kairat should push at home as they need the win, but Mjällby, the fresher in-season side, can keep the ball, which the near-even split (4.4 to 4.3) already reflects, so I stay at 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards, already taking a little off for referee Paweł Raczkowski (3.8 cards a game in six on record) and for Mjällby's tidy recent record. There is no rivalry between the clubs; a Kairat side that must win could foul more if they fall behind, but that is only a hunch, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots and already take about 7% off Kairat for their low recent shooting. I trim a little more, to about 24.1, because Kairat have had no competitive game for around three weeks under an interim coach, and Mjällby may be without Bergström and could rotate after the long trip with a league finale on Sunday; the numbers can't see either.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already cutting Kairat by about 10% for only 14 on target in six and lifting Mjällby for their accurate recent shooting. Kairat's lack of match rhythm and the doubt over Bergström, Mjällby's joint top scorer, point a little lower, so I go to about 8.1.
